transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-09
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Ravi (Saffron), Elena (Saffron), Samir (Saffron), Nora (Saffron), Tomas (Saffron)

Summary (auto):
Quick scoping call to align on POC success criteria for private-networked deployment. Main topics: workload sizing, benchmark metrics (latency/throughput/cost), connectivity options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), region and egress constraints, timeline and next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh happy to, yeah um to kick off. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on this account. Priya and Jordan from our eng team are on for the deep technical bits.
[00:18] Ravi: Hey Alex, thanks. We'll keep this tight — Saffron's goal is to run a 6-week pilot to validate we can meet latency and residency constraints before committing to a reserved capacity.
[00:28] Priya: Great, can you walk me through the workload? typical sequence lengths, concurrency, is this mostly embeddings, chat, or batch scoring?
[00:38] Nora: Mostly real-time inference for a customer-facing insights product. 70% chat-style short prompts (avg 120 tokens), 20% reranking/semantic search (embeddings), 10% batch scoring during off-peak. Peak concurrency expected ~180-250 requests per second, bursty from 3-6pm local.
[00:57] Elena: And just to reiterate, data residency: all PII and derived features must not leave eu-west-1. We need private connectivity and egress blocked to public internet except to Redwood control-plane endpoints.
[01:12] Priya: OK that's clear. For private connectivity we typically offer two patterns: VPC peering (fast, simple) or PrivateLink (more controlled egress and IAM boundaries). Each has tradeoffs around cross-account routing and supported regions.
[01:30] Tomas: If we do VPC peering, we want to avoid transitive routing through other peered VPCs. Also curious about latency impact of peering vs PrivateLink, we have a P50 target of 120ms end-to-end from app to tokenized response. P95 under 300ms would be acceptable for initial pilot.
[01:48] Jordan: Right, so a few things to note, the P50/P95 depends a lot on warm KV-cache and batch size. For short prompts like 120 tokens, our runtime with prefix caching typically hits P50s in the 60-110ms range on comparable GPUs, but that assumes a warmed KV and steady batching. Cold-start or large model variants push that up.
[02:10] Samir: Security-wise we need: SOC2 attestation, encryption in transit and at rest with customer-managed KMS, SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also the security questionnaire — we filled the first half but there's an outstanding ops question about key rotation.
[02:29] Maya: We can provide SOC2 report and SAML setup instructions; KMS integration is supported in our Private deployment and for Dedicated we can integrate customer KMS via KMS grants. We'll attach the security pack after the call.
[02:44] Ravi: Good. On benchmarks, what metrics do you want us to focus on so the execs will green-light a Dedicated commit?
[02:51] Priya: Success criteria suggestions: 1) End-to-end P50 < 150ms and P95 < 350ms for 120-token chat at pilot load; 2) Sustained throughput 200 req/s with <2% tail errors for 10-minute windows; 3) No egress to non-EU regions; 4) Integration with customer KMS and SSO in pilot window; 5) Observable cost per 1k tokens below our projected threshold (we'll produce an estimate).
[03:18] Nora: The exec asks for cost per 1k tokens target — we can share a rough number, but we need Redwood's estimate for caching and batching benefits since we expect heavy prefix reuse.
[03:28] Priya: We'll run tests with and without prefix cache to show delta; also provide quantization profiles if you want to test smaller variants. We'll include token-level cost breakdown in the spreadsheet.
[03:40] Elena: For connectivity, my infra lead needs an architecture diagram. Can you send one that shows both peering and PrivateLink flows and the required route table changes?
[03:50] Alex: Absolutely, we'll share a PrivateLink diagram and a VPC peering diagram. Note: PrivateLink requires an endpoint service on our side and an endpoint in your VPC; route tables are minimal but you need to allow specific security group flows. For peering, you'll need to ensure no overlapping CIDRs and we recommend dedicated peering for the pilot to avoid transitive complexity.
[04:12] Tomas: On egress constraints — can Redwood's runtime run in eu-west-1 and ensure egress only to customer-managed storage/Control Plane endpoints? We want to block any outbound to external S3 buckets in us-east.
[04:25] Jordan: Yes — for Private deployments we can keep everything in eu-west-1. For Redwood Hosted endpoints we can route data through a PrivateLink into your VPC so logs and artifacts never traverse public internet. We'll also provide an egress whitelist for required control-plane callbacks.
[04:40] Samir: Regarding audit logs, we want 90 days retention in our SIEM and the ability to query per-request metadata (model id, user token hash, latency). Is that supported?
[04:50] Maya: We can ship request-level events through a Kinesis/CloudWatch subscription or S3 (depending on your preference) — we'll work with your security team on the schema. 90 days is fine as long as it's in your account.
[05:02] Ravi: Timeline — we have internal stake holders and are targeting a pilot start in two weeks. Is that feasible?
[05:10] Alex: Two weeks is aggressive but doable if we get the VPC information and security checklist filled out quickly. Typical timeline we propose: Week 0 (this week) share docs & bench plan; Week 1 configure PrivateLink/peering and run connectivity sanity tests; Week 2 run baseline perf (cold and warm); Week 3 tune batching/cache and run sustained throughput tests; Week 4-5 run production-like scenarios and finalize success metrics; Week 6 exec review and decision.
[05:36] Elena: That aligns with our schedule but we need Redwood to own the bench harness or give us an executable harness so our devops can run it inside the dev VPC.
[05:46] Priya: We'll provide a containerized harness and a CloudFormation/Terraform module to deploy the test runner in your VPC. We'll also provide sample scripts for generating realistic prompt mixes (chat/embedding/batch).
[05:58] Nora: For the benchmark, can you include both PrivateLink and peering runs so we can compare latency differences?
[06:04] Jordan: Yes, we'll script both. Expect latency delta small but measurable: PrivateLink adds an extra hop but provides tighter IAM and egress control; peering is slightly lower P50 but can be less flexible for cross-account control. We'll capture both in the spreadsheet.
[06:22] Tomas: On throughput: you mentioned 200 req/s sustained — what GPU footprint should we expect in Dedicated if we later commit?
[06:30] Priya: Tentative rule of thumb: for medium-size models with quantization and batching, one A100-80GB equiv can sustain 400-600 tokens/sec depending on workmix; for latency-sensitive small prompts you'll need more instances to keep P95 tight. We'll produce an estimated capacity table for the pilot outcomes.
[06:48] Samir: Any additional controls for egress encryption and HSM? We need HSM-backed KMS for production — pilot can use narrower keys but must show path to HSM.
[06:59] Maya: We support customer-managed KMS with HSM in our Private product and for Dedicated we can integrate with your HSM provider. Pilot can use standard KMS with rotation policy, we'll document the upgrade path.
[07:12] Alex: Quick note on benchmarks — we'll capture: 1) cold vs warm latency curves, 2) P50/P95/P99, 3) throughput sustainability, 4) error and retry budgets, 5) token-level cost. We'll fill those columns in the shared spreadsheet. Link: https://redwood.example.com/saffron/pilot-bench (placeholder).
[07:31] Ravi: Sounds good. A few questions from procurement: are there any early-termination penalties for Dedicated if we convert from pilot to reserved and then want to change region?
[07:41] Alex: That's a contractual detail but generally region changes require migration planning; we can discuss contract language in the next legal touchpoint. For pilot there is no early-termination fee — we'll provide an optional priced path for Dedicated in the follow-up.
[07:55] Elena: For debugging, do you provide request tracing that contains redacted user content but full latency traces? We need traces correlated to our trace IDs.
[08:04] Jordan: Yes — we can ingest trace IDs if your app passes them as headers; our tracing attaches request-level metadata while honoring redaction policies. We'll show an example tracing config in the ops doc.
[08:17] Priya: Another practical thing — sequence length distribution matters. If you can share a sample of 2000 anonymized prompts (no PII, hashed IDs), we can run synthetic runs that match your mix.
[08:29] Nora: We can prepare that; we'll scrub and hash.
[08:34] Samir: On regulatory side, we need data residency proof for audits — can you provide a signed statement that logs and inference data will remain in eu-west-1 for the pilot?
[08:44] Maya: We can provide a residency addendum for the pilot and capture logs in your account. We'll confirm language with legal and share a draft.
[08:53] Alex: Great. Any blockers left?
[08:56] Ravi: One small one — latency monitors. We want synthetic monitors from multiple EU zones to validate global UX. Can Redwood run synthetic checks or will we run them?
[09:07] Jordan: We can run synthetic monitors and share dashboards, or provide the API end points for you to run your own; we typically do both for pilots.
[09:15] Elena: Cost sensitivity — our CFO wants a conservative and an optimistic cost scenario in the spreadsheet. Can Redwood produce two cost curves (with and without prefix caching)?
[09:25] Priya: Yes, we'll produce conservative/optimistic and show the caching delta.
[09:30] Alex: Ok let's recap next steps before we wrap.
[09:32] Alex: Redwood will: (1) Send PrivateLink and VPC peering architecture diagrams and checklist (Alex) by 2026-06-10; (2) Provide a benchmark plan, harness container, and test scripts (Priya) by 2026-06-11; (3) Share security pack and SOC2 report (Maya) by 2026-06-10; (4) Populate cost scenarios in bench spreadsheet and share link (Jordan/Priya) by 2026-06-11.
[09:57] Alex: Saffron will: (1) Provide dev VPC CIDR and peering contact (Elena) by 2026-06-12; (2) Share anonymized prompt samples (Nora) by 2026-06-12; (3) Complete outstanding items on security questionnaire (Samir) by 2026-06-12.
[10:15] Ravi: OK those timelines are OK. We'll aim to have the dev VPC open and the peering contact assigned by Friday.
[10:22] Nora: Small note — for the bench runs please log request id and model hash for each sample so we can reproduce any anomalies.
[10:31] Jordan: Will do. We'll include request-id and model-id in the logging schema.
[10:35] Priya: One more technical nuance — if you have bursts >300 RPS we recommend a small buffer on autoscaling during the pilot; we'll add suggested autoscale policy in the ops doc.
[10:48] Tomas: Good. Anything else from anyone?
[10:52] Samir: No, just please include KMS rotation details.
[10:56] Maya: We'll include rotation and HSM upgrade path.
[11:00] Alex: Great, thank you everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and the bench link; scheduling the bench run for week of 2026-06-16 — I'll send a calendar invite with a pre-checklist.
[11:12] Ravi: Thanks all. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
[11:15] (call ends)
